question: What does the Act say about discrimination?

answer_full:
The Discrimination against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act outlaws discrimination on the basis of one's physical, mental or sensory impairment [Factsheet general]. The Act, signed into law in January 2019, sets up a National Commission for Persons with Disabilities to oversee the inclusivity of persons with disabilities in society [Factsheet general]. The Act outlaws discrimination in its totality and under any manner or circumstance [Factsheet Section 2].

Specifically, a person with disability shall not be discriminated against on the ground of his disability [Act cl. 1]. This prohibits the discrimination of a person on the ground of his/her disability, as stated in section 1(1) [Factsheet Section 1]. A person who contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence [Act cl. 1]. If the person is a body corporate, they are liable on conviction to a fine of N1,000,000 [Act cl. 1]. If the person is an individual, they are liable to a fine of N100,000 or six months imprisonment [Act cl. 1]. A body corporate who discriminates on this ground is subject to a fine of N1,000,000 [Factsheet Section 1]. An individual is liable to pay a N100,000 fine, face a six months imprisonment term or both [Factsheet Section 1].

A civil action may also be brought by the person discriminated against [Factsheet Section 1] [Factsheet Section 2]. The Act provides for the full integration of persons with disabilities into society and establishes the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities, vesting it with responsibilities for their education, health care, social, economic, and civil rights [Act general].

question: Are public buildings required to be accessible?
answer_excerpt: Yes, public buildings are required to be accessible. answer_full:
Yes, public buildings are required to be accessible. A person with disability has the right to access the physical environment and buildings on an equal basis with others [Act cl. 3,4,5]. Public buildings shall be constructed with necessary accessibility aids such as lifts (where necessary), ramps and any other facility that makes them accessible to and usable by persons with disabilities [Act cl. 3,4,5].

There is a transitory period of five years from the commencement of the Act within which all public buildings and structures, whether immovable, movable, or automobile, that were inaccessible to persons with disabilities shall be modified to be accessible to and usable by persons with disabilities, including those on wheelchairs [Act cl. 6,7]. This gives a five years transitory period within which all public buildings or structures whether immovable or not must be modified and accessible to persons with disabilities including those on wheelchairs [Factsheet Section 6,7].

Before erecting any public structure, its plan shall be scrutinised by the relevant authority to ensure that the plan conforms with the building code [Act cl. 6,7]. A government or government agency, body or individual responsible for the approval of building plans shall not approve the plan of a public building if the plan does not make provision for accessibility facilities [Act cl. 6,7]. This provides the procedure for erecting public structures, so it conforms with a building code that has accessibility features for persons with disabilities including those on wheelchair [Factsheet Section 7]. Section 7(2) prohibits government bodies, agencies or individuals responsible for the approval of building plans from approving plans without accessibility features [Factsheet Section 7].

question: What employment protections exist for persons with disabilities?
answer_excerpt: All employers of labour in public organisations shall, as much as possible, have persons with disabilities constituting at least 5% of their employment [Act cl. 29,30]. Contravention of this provision is liable to N50,000 damages payable to the affected person with disability [Act cl. 29,30].
answer_full: All employers of labour in public organisations shall, as much as possible, have persons with disabilities constituting at least 5% of their employment [Act cl. 29,30]. Contravention of this provision is liable to N50,000 damages payable to the affected person with disability [Act cl. 29,30].

question: Is there a commission for persons with disabilities?
answer_excerpt: Yes, there is a National Commission for Persons with Disabilities established [Act cl. 31] [Act general] [Factsheet Section 30,31]. This Commission is placed under the Presidency [Act cl. 31]. The Act provides for its establishment and vests it with responsibilities for the education, health care, social, economic, and civil rights of persons with disabilities [Act general].
answer_full: Yes, there is a National Commission for Persons with Disabilities established [Act cl. 31] [Act general] [Factsheet Section 30,31]. This Commission is placed under the Presidency [Act cl. 31]. The Act provides for its establishment and vests it with responsibilities for the education, health care, social, economic, and civil rights of persons with disabilities [Act general].

question: Does the Act cover access to vehicles and transport?
answer_excerpt: Yes, the Discrimination against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act covers access to vehicles and transport. The Discrimination against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act outlaws discrimination on the basis of one’s physical, mental or sensory impairment [Factsheet general]. The Act mandates government providers to make provisions for lifts, ramps and other accessibility aids that enhance the accessibility of their vehicles, parks and bus stops to persons with disabilities [Factsheet Section 10]. Section 10(1) mandates provisions for lifts, ramps and other accessibility aids a...
answer_full:
Yes, the Discrimination against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act covers access to vehicles and transport.

The Discrimination against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act outlaws discrimination on the basis of one’s physical, mental or sensory impairment [Factsheet general]. The Act mandates government providers to make provisions for lifts, ramps and other accessibility aids that enhance the accessibility of their vehicles, parks and bus stops to persons with disabilities [Factsheet Section 10]. Section 10(1) mandates provisions for lifts, ramps and other accessibility aids at public vehicles, parks and bus stops to persons with disabilities [Factsheet Section 10,11]. Every public vehicle is mandated to have functional audible and visual display of their destination within five years of commencement of this Act [Factsheet Section 10,11]. Similar provisions are made in section 11 for all transport service providers [Factsheet Section 10,11].

Specifically, transport service providers shall make provisions for lifts, ramps and other accessibility facilities and aids to enhance the accessibility of their vehicles, parks and bus stops to persons with disabilities, including those on wheelchairs [Act cl. 11]. Every public vehicle shall have functional audible and visual display of their destination within five years from the commencement of this Act [Act cl. 11]. Lifts, ramps and all other accessibility equipment in or for vehicles, and at parks or bus stops, shall be maintained in operational condition [Act cl. 11]. Section 11 also mandates the regular and frequent maintenance of accessibility aids and equipment in vehicles [Factsheet Section 10,11]. Additionally, section 11(4) places a duty of care on a drive [Factsheet Section 10,11].

question: What rights do children with disabilities have to education?
answer_excerpt: Children with disabilities, as persons with disabilities, have an unfettered right to education without discrimination or segregation in any form [Act cl. 16,17]. A person with disability is entitled to free education [Act cl. 16,17], specifically up to secondary level [Factsheet Section 17]. This right to education is free from discrimination [Factsheet Section 17]. Section 17 provides for the right to free education [Factsheet Section 19,17,20]. The National Commission for Persons with Disabilities is mandated to provide educational assistive devices [Factsheet Section 17]. The Government sh...
answer_full:
Children with disabilities, as persons with disabilities, have an unfettered right to education without discrimination or segregation in any form [Act cl. 16,17]. A person with disability is entitled to free education [Act cl. 16,17], specifically up to secondary level [Factsheet Section 17]. This right to education is free from discrimination [Factsheet Section 17]. Section 17 provides for the right to free education [Factsheet Section 19,17,20]. The National Commission for Persons with Disabilities is mandated to provide educational assistive devices [Factsheet Section 17].

The Government shall ensure that the education of persons with disabilities, particularly children who are blind, deaf or with multiple disabilities, is delivered in the most appropriate language, mode and means of communication for the individual, and in environments which maximise academic and social development [Act cl. 20]. Section 20 of the Act provides for the appropriate mode of education for persons with disabilities, especially children [Factsheet Section 19,17,20].

Education is to be inclusive, as provided by Section 18 [Act general], which compliments the right to free education [Factsheet Section 19,17,20]. Section 19 provides for subsidised education for special education personnel [Act general], which helps to provide such education [Factsheet Section 19,17,20].

question: How long is the transitional compliance period?
answer_excerpt: A five years transitory period is given for all public buildings or structures to be modified and accessible to persons with disabilities, including those on wheelchairs [Factsheet Section 6,7].
answer_full: A five years transitory period is given for all public buildings or structures to be modified and accessible to persons with disabilities, including those on wheelchairs [Factsheet Section 6,7].

question: Does the Constitution guarantee dignity and equality?
answer_excerpt: The Constitution states that the State social order is founded on ideals of Equality [Constitution s. 17]. It also states that every citizen shall have equality of rights, obligations and opportunities before the law [Constitution s. 17]. The sanctity of the human person shall be recognised and human dignity shall [Constitution s. 17]. There is a Right to dignity of human persons [Constitution s. 33].
answer_full: The Constitution states that the State social order is founded on ideals of Equality [Constitution s. 17]. It also states that every citizen shall have equality of rights, obligations and opportunities before the law [Constitution s. 17]. The sanctity of the human person shall be recognised and human dignity shall [Constitution s. 17]. There is a Right to dignity of human persons [Constitution s. 33].
